desc: Dusk café façade establishing; Noah walks toward the door; slow push-in.
Inside café: patron whispers a secret to another (Every secret. Every lie.).
Outside: a girl glances at a boy; tiny pink "?" thought (what your crush thinks).
Morning bedroom: alarm rings, Noah's eyes snap open and he sits up; a violet shimmer = the power arrives.
Over Noah's shoulder: smiling barista hands him a coffee ("Here you go!").
Barista keeps smiling (mouth closed) while a violet thought pops behind her: "Please don't spill it."
Extreme close-up of Noah's eyes widening; pupils reflect the barista and the falling cup ("WHAT THE—").
Low-angle slow motion: the cup tumbles, time FREEZES (violet pulse), then resumes falling.
Floor-level: the cup smashes; coffee splashes, shards scatter.
Barista looks down in horror, hands to chest; thought: "I'm getting fired."
Title card over the café façade: "WHAT IF YOU COULD HEAR EVERYONE'S THOUGHTS?"
Noah clutches his head outside the café; faint whisper ghosts swirl ("losing his mind").
Wide: Noah steps onto the morning street; a tiny "..." thought pops above every passer-by.
Side-tracking: businessman on phone says "Almost at the office"; his thought window shows the boss tapping a foot beside a clock.
Woman passes; holographic window with a glowing oven: "Did I leave the oven on?"
Snap zoom onto a man in a flat cap staring right back at Noah: "Why is that kid staring at me?"
Close-up: Noah grins in disbelief — "Oh my god. This is actually real."
Classroom: Noah taps his temple smugly; small thoughts pop over bored classmates.
Wide classroom: teacher at the chalkboard, Noah near the back.
Teacher (glasses) points: "Noah. What's the answer to question seven?"
Close-up: Noah freezes, nervous — "Uh..."
Room desaturates; teacher's thought "It's B" — a luminous B floats across the room and lands above Noah's desk.
Noah shoots his hand up: "B!"
Smash cut: the teacher, stunned — "...Correct."
Three-beat montage: Noah answers again and again; glowing answers "x = 7", "1776", "H₂O" (VO: school wasn't so difficult).
Insert: the classroom clock hits 3:00 as the bell rings.
Busy school hallway: Noah walks through, confident; blurred students pass in the foreground.
One-point corridor: Maya stands in a pool of warm light at the far end (label: MAYA).
Comedic: Noah hides behind an open locker door, peeking out nervously (too scared for a year).
Long-lens push from behind Noah toward Maya; focus racks from Noah to Maya as the distance compresses.
Maya glances over; a pink handwritten thought (with tiny hearts): "Wait... Noah actually looks kinda cute today."
Noah's eyes go wide — whispers "No way" — then a triumphant fist-pump grin with sparkles.
Maya tilts her head, puzzled; a cooler blue thought: "Why is he smiling like that?"
Hard cut: Noah freezes into a painfully awkward grin and looks away — "Oh." (record scratch).
Noah struts down the hallway with sparkles — "luckiest person alive".
From behind Noah: he pushes the CAFETERIA double doors open — warm light and a crowd beyond.
Locked behind Noah: every student has a thought shape above their head; they multiply and overlap.
Noah, worried ("Wait, hold on—"), as overlapping thought windows crowd in; camera pushes into them until violet fills the screen.
Camera orbits Noah as the cafeteria stretches into an infinite violet space full of layered thought panels.
Overhead: rows of students, a thought window pops over every head; counter ticks to "200 THOUGHTS".
Close-up: Noah winces, deadpan, boxed in by thought windows ("Not so much.").
Students at a table, mouths shut, thoughts popping: "I'm starving." / "Why did she leave me on read?" / "I hate Mondays."
Another table: "Did I fail chemistry?" / "Does anyone even like me?" / "Is my hair weird today?"
Orbit tightens on Noah covering his ears as panels multiply around him ("couldn't turn any of it off").
Overload peak: rapid cuts — Noah's eyes, hands over ears, overhead of countless windows — then a hard cut to black silence.
Extreme close-up: Noah's hands pressed over his ears; violet thought-lines keep streaming past ("Nothing.").
Profile: Noah in huge headphones; the thought lines pass straight through them ("Still nothing.").
Wide symmetrical bathroom: Noah alone in the centre while glowing thought windows drift straight through the walls.
Low angle: Noah throws his arms up and shouts at the ceiling — "ARE YOU KIDDING ME?"
A calm, ordinary hallway (no effects): Noah slumps at his open locker, exhausted.
Insert: a photo taped inside the locker — young Noah and Leo laughing, "best friends forever (age 8)".
Stable two-shot: Leo (green cap) strolls in, taps Noah's shoulder — "Yo, you coming over Friday?"
Close on Noah; the hallway darkens; Leo's thought appears word by word beside him: "I can't keep doing this."
Two-shot: Noah asks "...Doing what?" — Leo, confused: "What?"
Close on Leo, looking down, unaware Noah can hear: "I have to tell him. He's gonna hate me." Silence after.
Noah at his desk, chin in hand, worried; Leo's two thoughts echo and drift around him.
Library: Leo quickly snaps his laptop shut as Noah walks up ("Was Leo planning to ditch him?").
Over Noah's shoulder: Leo laughs on the phone, sees Noah, hangs up abruptly with an awkward smile ("lying this whole time?").
Leo at his locker with Noah hovering behind; Leo's thought: "I wish he'd stop asking."
Leo, determined; his thought window shows a calendar with FRIDAY circled: "Friday. I have to do it Friday."
Leo walks away; behind him, Noah's imagined fears appear as grainy grey torn panels (Leo ditching him, laughing behind his back, Noah alone on Friday) — speculation, not real thoughts.
Close two-shot: Maya gently reaches toward Noah — "Hey, Noah. You okay?" — he's still buried in harsh purple thought-noise.
Maya, concerned; her thought is soft and warm-coloured: "He seems really upset."
Noah, arms crossed, avoiding her eyes — "I'm fine." — purple noise all around him.
Over Noah's shoulder on Maya: "I want to help, but I don't know what to say." — Noah snaps "Then don't say ANYTHING!" and every overlay vanishes.
Clean, ordinary frame — no overlays: Maya, hurt and confused, "...What?" Held for a full beat.
Wide: Maya walks off; Noah left alone in the empty hallway, regretful.
Close on Noah looking down at his hands; labels HEAR ≠ UNDERSTAND fade in (VO: hearing a thought didn't mean he understood it).
Insert: the classroom clock ticks toward the end of Thursday.
Dusk, school entrance: over Noah's shoulder (blurred FG) we watch Leo walk away down the street.
Leo walking in the sunset, anxious; thought: "Tomorrow's going to change everything."
Night: Noah lies awake; a date graphic flips THURSDAY 11:59 PM → FRIDAY 12:00 AM over the low clock tick.
Extreme wide, nearly empty courtyard (Friday): Noah waits under a big tree, arms crossed; Leo approaches from far away. Held.
Camera creeps closer as Leo reaches Noah; the friends occupy opposite sides of the frame.
Medium two-shot, wide gap between them: Noah — "So. What were you gonna tell me?" Leo — "What?"
Over Leo's shoulder: Noah, cold — "Don't act like you don't know."
Over Noah's shoulder: Leo panics silently; a subdued violet thought behind him — "Oh no. Not like this."
Camera tracks around the pair: Noah accuses ("You've been hiding something from me all week"); Leo pleads ("just let me explain").
Sharp close-up of Noah's eyes; Leo's thought "He's gonna think I'm abandoning him" is projected across his face.
Noah, angry and hurt, repeats the private thought aloud: "So you ARE abandoning me?"
Extreme close-up on Leo: his eyes widen, mouth falls open — "How did you—"
Noah blurts out his secret: "I KNOW what you're thinking, Leo!"
Silence. The camera pulls back to a wide: a big empty gap of courtyard between the two friends.
Leo pulls a folded letter from his bag and holds it out: "I got accepted into a school overseas."
Noah, all the anger draining away — "...What?"
Insert: the acceptance letter — "ASHFORD INTERNATIONAL ACADEMY, London · FULL SCHOLARSHIP · Departure: Sunday, August 30".
Wider two-shot with the letter between them: Noah — "And you were just gonna leave without telling me?" Leo — "No! I was trying to figure out HOW to tell you."
Leo, earnest and scared; his last thought glows faintly then fades away: "Please just be happy for me." (violet overlays fade out of the film here).
Eye-level close-up, golden light: Noah, quietly — "You said you couldn't keep doing this."
Leo, embarrassed and sad: "Yeah. Pretending everything was normal… while I knew I was leaving."
Noah looks down at the letter in his hands: "And you thought I'd hate you?"
Leo, voice trembling: "I was scared you'd think I chose a new life over being your friend."
Brief warm memory: young Noah and Leo (age 8) laughing, kicking a ball in a golden park.
Back on Leo, a small sincere look: "I wanted you to be the first person I told." Music enters after the line.
Noah's face softens as he understands ("And suddenly, Noah understood.").
Revisit: Maya — SAID "You okay?" + THOUGHT "I want to help…" → MEANT "She cared about him."
Revisit: Teacher — SAID "What's the answer?" + THOUGHT "Please don't say C again." → MEANT "She was rooting for him."
Revisit: Leo — SAID "Coming over Friday?" + THOUGHT "He's gonna hate me." → MEANT "He was scared of losing his best friend."
Noah looks at the letter, then up ("He could hear what people were thinking…").
Wide, golden courtyard, no text on screen: the two friends standing closer now ("He still didn't know what they meant.").
Noah breaks into a grin: "Dude. You're actually getting a FULL scholarship?" Faint thought windows linger, blurred, in the background — he ignores them.
Leo, shy smile: "Yeah."
Two-shot, now standing close: "That's insane! Why didn't you just tell me?" — Leo laughs: "I was TRYING to."
Noah, sincere: "...I'm happy for you, man."
Leo relaxes into a laugh; a tiny, faint thought ("Thank god.") appears small and soft — Noah doesn't react to it.
A small, slightly awkward hug; the camera slowly pulls out to the wide courtyard composition from the start of Act 3.
School entrance in warm late-afternoon light: Noah walks down the steps ("one person he was too scared to ask about").
Maya enters from the left; Noah turns to her — "Hey. You want to walk home together?"
Maya, nervous smile; a small understated thought: "Please say yes."
Hold on Noah's genuine smile — he answers what she SAID: "Yeah. I'd like that."
Wide sunset street: Noah and Maya walk off together.
End card: "What would YOU do if you could hear everyone's thoughts?" with the cast line-up.
